description:
Two shepherd-d tests that each call `libp2p.New` via [transport/libp2p].New trip Go's race detector when run in the same test binary with `-race`, even when they don't share state. The race report points into go-libp2p's `fx`-driven host construction.

Reproducer (verified against mosey `v0.0.0-20260522075807-017a918adfd5`): run shepherd's `./cmd/shepherd-d/...` with `-race -count=1` after [adding a third test](https://github.com/firefly-engineering/shepherd) that calls `startLibp2p` while the other two were already parallel. Two tests pass, three race.

Trace bottom (truncated to the mosey + upstream frames):

```
github.com/firefly-engineering/mosey/transport/libp2p.New()
    .../mosey/transport/libp2p/libp2p.go:135 +0x630
github.com/libp2p/go-libp2p.New()
github.com/libp2p/go-libp2p.NewWithoutDefaults()
github.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/config.(*Config).NewNode()
go.uber.org/fx.New()
go.uber.org/fx.(*module).invokeAll()
```

The downstream symptom is that shepherd CI either pins this to a single-threaded test or skips the race variant via a build tag — neither great, but workable while this is open.

Possible angles to investigate:
1. Confirm whether the race is inside go-libp2p's package-level init (`init()` registering with fx) or in mosey's own setup path. If upstream, file a go-libp2p issue and link from here.
2. If mosey's `libp2p.New` is reading any package-global on a non-init path, gate that read with sync.Once or a mutex.
3. Document the constraint in [`transport/libp2p/doc.go`](transport/libp2p/doc.go): "concurrent New is race-unsafe under -race; use `sync.Mutex` across calls in test code that does this."

Low priority because it's a -race-only diagnostic, but worth resolving before the next consumer trips on it.

comments.text: Filed shep-wo5 in firefly-engineering/shepherd asking for a precise repro — current shepherd repro instructions weren't enough to reproduce here (tried 3+ concurrent New, with and without DHT, on darwin/arm64 Go 1.26 against go-libp2p v0.48.0 — clean). Picked up one extra clue: shepherd's racing test (internal/pubsub/libp2p_test.go) calls libp2pgo.New directly, not via mosey, so this is unambiguously upstream and not anything in mosey's wrapper path. Holding ship-y65 until shep-wo5 lands a minimal repro.

Resolved as 'not a mosey bug'. After bypassing the t.Skip in shepherd's TestRun_Libp2pWithCert and capturing the full race report, the racing operations are:

  Read:  bytes.(*Buffer).String() — test reads errOut.String() at main_test.go:248
  Write: bytes.(*Buffer).Write() via slog.TextHandler — shepherd's gRPC Serve goroutine logging at server.go:229, spawned from main.go:320

bytes.Buffer is not concurrent-safe; the test reads it while a background goroutine spawned by run() is still writing to it via slog. The deep mosey/libp2p/fx frames in the original trace are the goroutine SPAWN chain (the writing goroutine was created inside fx wiring during libp2pbackend.New), not the racing code — Go's race detector lists goroutine ancestry in 'created at' which is easy to misread as the race site.

Fix is on the shepherd side: wait for Serve's goroutine to exit before run() returns. Filed shep-wo5 with the diagnosis + fix options.

Closing ship-y65 as 'not a mosey issue' — no mosey-side docs / serialization / upstream report needed.

title: Race detector flags concurrent libp2p.New() across same-binary tests
